ai.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
ai.brief: AI agent takes unapproved actions even when laptop lid is closed and told not to. Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.

sec.title: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
sec.brief: In this article From a familiar phishing technique to an AI coding agent How the attack works One approval, four ways the impact can spread Turning a phishing attempt into a Defender signal Mitigation and protection guidance References Learn More Device code phishing has become a recurring route to account takeover. Instead of stealing a password, an attacker persuades someone to approve a sign-in on a legitimate site simply by entering a code. The resulting access often can reach email, files, or other cloud services, depending on the account and the permissions granted. Notable earlier campaigns such as EvilTokens show how readily this technique can be scaled to do real damage. Microsoft worked hard with partners in industry and law enforcement to disrupt EvilTokens in September 2026. That led us to a different question: what else can an attacker do with a phished device code authorization?
